programs.name: Hounslow Classic: Marathon 43km
programs.tagline: Starting at Allview Escape, runners make their way across the stony clifftops to the Grand Canyon, heading clockwise through the canyon to Evans Lookout, descending into carved canyon walls and swirling pools, then climbing back to Neates Glen and the Grand Canyon Aid Station before returning to Allview Escape for Round 2. The second part is the famous out-and-back to the Pinnacles via Perrys Lookdown, plunging into the Grose Wilderness to the Giant Blue Gum Forest, crossing Govetts Creek and ascending to Lockleys Pylon, traversing to the Pinnacles Aid Station, then returning up the steps of Perrys Lookdown to the finish.

programs.name: Hounslow 17km - 12 weeks
programs.tagline:
A 12-week program built specifically for the Hounslow Classic 17km. With 900m of vertical in only 17km, an average gradient of 53m per kilometre and a sustained technical descent through the Grand Canyon, this is sky-running terrain. The program prepares you for what the course actually asks of you.
Starting at Allview Escape, runners make their way across the stony clifftops to the Grand Canyon, descending into ancient canyon trails before returning to reset for Round 2: the famous out-and-back to the Pinnacles via Perrys Lookdown, the Blue Gum Forest, and Lockleys Pylon. Technical Blue Mountains terrain with major climbs.

programs.name: UTMB Kosci 100km
programs.tagline: 100km race starting and finishing at Friday Flat, Thredbo, Kosciuszko National Park. Start time 7:30am. Kosci100 is a runnable alpine 100K. The program is built to develop aerobic durability first, then layer in the skills that determine whether an amateur athlete can keep moving well for up to 28 hours: fuelling, power hiking, low-light confidence, alpine kit fluency, downhill resilience, decision-making under fatigue and energy availability protection. This is not a mileage contest. It is a 20-week progression in becoming organised, durable, fuelled and calm enough to execute a long alpine race.

programs.name: Grampians Peaks Trail: 100 Mile Team Relay [continuous] (4 person)
programs.tagline:
Teams of four will tackle the 100 mile course running alongside the solo competitors.

The Legs of the team’s race will be the same as the stage race, where teams will relay at the three major aid stations in Halls Gap, Mt William Carpark and Griffin Fireline.

Teams will have to play to each other’s strengths with some legs being longer or at night. Night runners will get to experience the beauty of the Grampians in the dark while being fresh, and able to absorb the nature and landscapes they run through.

If one or more runner cannot complete their leg, we will be flexible in letting the other runners share the load in completing the full course.

Teams in the Miler Team Relay will be responsible for transporting their next runner to the changeover points. The first runner can get the shuttle to the start and the last runner can get the shuttle back to Halls Gap if required.

It is highly encouraged that teams book accomodation in Halls Gap from Thursday to Monday as this will be where the event village is and all the shuttles will leave from and return to the Event Village at Centenary Hall.

The first Leg to Halls Gap starts with the iconic climb up Flat Rock to reveal the entirety of the world famous Taipan Wall. After running under the rock wall the trail finds its groove as it toggles between a thin rocky uneven surface and a smooth dirt ribbon. There are numerous waterfalls through here, with continual 360 views of the entire Grampians grandeur, which is a common theme throughout the whole run.

The second Leg through to Duwul/Mt William has continual long climbs. It may be nightfall for the majority of the field heading up to the famous Pinnacles Lookout or Mount Rosea. This section is draining with foot placement and ankle stability being the key. Conserve energy when possible. Take time at Borough Huts to compose yourself and fuel and hydrate. The next 15km to Mt William are the crux of the race. There is much technical trail, especially up to, and across the Seven Dials and Redmans Bluff. However, the trail improves from here and the views from the top are spectacular as the trail adheres to a clifftop along to Mt William Aid Station. 

The third Leg through to Griffin Fireline is a net downhill. Except for the speedy teams it will be into the daylight of Saturday for the bulk of the field to navigate this difficult stretch in the day. It starts with a very challenging 19k which crosses the Major Mitchell Plateau up to the high point of the race, Durd Durd at 1167m asl. A very long and initially steep descent brings you to Jimmy Creek where the runner will be rewarded for having done the hardest section of their race. Many short punchy climbs and flowy downs follow. There is a lot of newly built trail, and it is much appreciated. It will be hard to find rhythm through these shorter continual hills, with some rock hopping, choppy climbs mixed in with fast terrain.

The fourth Leg passes over some of the well-known peaks in the southern section of the range. This means lots of steep ascent, often on stairs to some striking summits including Mud-Dadjug/Mt Abrupt, and Wurgarri/Mt Sturgeon. Despite being a short Leg it has three big steep climbs with stairs. It is pound for pound the most scenic section of the route. Teams will have a sense of the journey’s end, which may bring joy but also sadness that the adventure must come to an end. Runners take an enjoyable river trail to the town centre, where the celebration awaits!

in summary - 
Unlike solo runners, team relay success hinges entirely on your vehicle choreography and timing at the three designated aid stations GPT100 Miler Team Relay | GRAMPIANS PEAKS TRAIL 100 MILER:Halls Gap (End of Leg 1 / Start of Leg 2): High energy, easy vehicle access, and the central basecamp of the event GPT100 Miler Team Relay | GRAMPIANS PEAKS TRAIL 100 MILER.Mt William Carpark (End of Leg 2 / Start of Leg 3): High elevation and highly exposed. Your incoming runner will experience rapid temperature drops; the crew must have heavy insulation ready Grampians Peak Trail: Section C4 - Duwul (Mt William) to Durd Durd.Griffin Fireline (End of Leg 3 / Start of Leg 4): Remote, deeper into the southern section, requiring precise navigation across open pasture transitions [Grampians Peaks Trail: Section S2 - Wannon to Djardji-djawara].

programs.name: Grampians Peaks Trail 100 mile Team Relay [Staged] (3 person)
programs.tagline: A 4-day stage race covering the full 162km Grampians Peaks Trail, from Mt Zero in the north to Dunkeld in the south. Teams of 3 each run one leg per day across the four stages. Stage 1 (Thu 6 Nov): Mt Zero to Halls Gap, 49.5km, 2000m+ - opens with the iconic Flat Rock climb and Taipan Wall, waterfalls and 360 views. Stage 2 (Fri 7 Nov): Halls Gap to Mt William Carpark, 37.5km, 2350m+ - hardest sustained climbing through Seven Dials and Redmans Bluff. Stage 3 (Sat 8 Nov): Mt William to Griffin Fireline, 42km, 1795m+, net downhill over Major Mitchell Plateau and Durd Durd high point (1167m). Stage 4 (Sun 9 Nov): Griffin Fireline to Dunkeld, 33km, 1555m+ - most scenic section over Signal Peak, Mt Abrupt and Mt Sturgeon to the Dunkeld finish.

programs.name: Roller Coaster Run: 12.4km
programs.tagline: The Roller Coaster 12km is a challenging twilight trail race through Victoria's Dandenong Ranges, starting from Kalorama Memorial Reserve. The course features steep singletrack climbs with punishing grades up to 35%, including the infamous Observatory Track, but rewards runners with sweeping Melbourne views from Burke's Lookout. After the peak, a fast and technical descent winds through lush fern rainforests and towering Mountain Ash trees before leading back to an energetic, party-vibe finish line. Aggressive trail running shoes are essential to tackle the loose terrain, and participants should expect a slower pace than standard road races due to the relentless "roller coaster" elevation profile.

programs.name: Surf Coast Century 100K Relay (team of 4)
programs.tagline:
This is your chance to take on a 100km ultra, as a team. In this four-person relay, each runner completes one leg of the course, experiencing a distinct slice of Victoria’s coastal and inland beauty.

Leg 1 (21km) features clifftop views and soft sand beaches. 

Leg 2 (28km) moves through forested singletrack and undulating inland trail. 

Leg 3 (28km) is the toughest: steep, technical, and the most elevation-heavy. 

Leg 4 (23km) closes with coastal views, rocky terrain, and the buzz of the finish line.

With ~1,800m total elevation, this event is a team-based challenge full of support, stoke, and story-worthy moments. Ideal for first-timers, friendship groups, or training crews looking to celebrate the trail together.
